verdict.rationale: Cline's docs say it builds features through natural conversation and makes coordinated multi-file changes with diffs and checkpoints. A CLI example shows it fixing failures from a plain-language prompt. Hands-on community reports confirm it can be set loose on a codebase and produce accurate diffs. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the multi-file editing workflow beyond homepage-level claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have the agent implement or fix it across multiple files

citations.quote: Coordinated multi-file changes with linter-aware fixes, diffs, checkpoints, and one-click undo on every step.
It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
cline --auto-approve true "run tests and fix failures"
I can plan with it for 10-15 minutes, set it loose on my codebase, go get lunch, and then its diff is almost always completely on the money.
